item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q009_heme_bundle_fold_not_homology","answer":"No. In SCOPe 2.08, all three are in the membrane-protein heme-binding four-helical-bundle fold f.21 (sunid 81344), but SCOPe assigns them to three separate superfamilies: transmembrane di-heme cytochromes, f.21.1 (sunid 81342); fumarate-reductase respiratory-complex transmembrane subunits, f.21.2 (sunid 81343); and respiratory nitrate-reductase 1 gamma chains, f.21.3 (sunid 103501). Thus SCOPe supports shared fold-level architecture, not a single homologous superfamily or probable common ancestry across all three. The common four-helix/heme-binding arrangement is insufficient for transferring substrate specificity, respiratory-complex role, redox mechanism, partner interactions, or detailed heme ligation. Cross-superfamily structures may serve as coarse topology/fold templates only; sequence alignment, helix registration, ligands, loops, and interfaces require independent validation. Representative sets should include each superfamily rather than using one member as representative of the whole fold. Any stronger homology claim would require external sequence-profile, structural-alignment, and phylogenetic evidence beyond shared fold membership.","evidence_used":["/api/v1/releases","/api/v1/","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=transmembrane%20di-heme","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=fumarate-reductase%20respiratory-complex%20transmembrane%20subunits&limit=10","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=respiratory%20nitrate-reductase%20gamma%20chains&limit=10","/api/v1/releases/2.08/search?q=fumarate%20reductase%20transmembrane&limit=20","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81344","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81342","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/81343","/api/v1/releases/2.08/sunids/103501"]}]}
